title: From Winning to Understanding: A Diagnostic Long-Horizon RTS Benchmark for LLMs
claim: A benchmark couples structured observations, an LLM decision agent, and a deterministic action interface to an environment in a closed feedback loop.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, with a feedback loop arrow above
description: A wide horizontal diagram of the LLM–OpenRA benchmark loop. On the left is a yellow Observation box listing game state: money, power, buildings, units and visible enemies. Next to it, a green dashed box holds the system prompt for the decision agent. In the middle are two player cards. Blue Player is a built-in rule-based or LLM agent, and Red Player is an LLM agent, each with a small tank icon. To their right, an orange Action box groups Build Commands (Produce Buildings, Produce Tanks) and Unit Commands (Move, Attack, Attack_move) as purple buttons. At the far right, a teal OpenRA Environment box states that it enforces RTS mechanics, exposes partial observations and logs metrics. Below it is a game screenshot. A thick black arrow along the bottom is labeled 'Decision & Execution Phase'. A black loop along the top is labeled 'Environment Feedback Phase' and returns to Observation.

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as decision modules, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of long-horizon, adversarial interaction while faithfully acting on human instructions. We introduce a long-horizon Red Alert RTS benchmark with a hierarchical interface in which LLMs output budgeted, low-frequency macro/tactical intents that are executed deterministically for standardized comparison. The benchmark evaluates (i) robustness to ``rules-as-variable'' perturbations via rule-style shifts , (ii) competitive strength via Elo-style ratings from head-to-head matches, and (iii) human steerability via standardized language interventions. Beyond win/loss, we log economy growth/spending, combat loss ratio, and visibility coverage to diagnose long-horizon failure modes. Overall, the benchmark provides a reproducible and diagnostic testbed for robustness and controllability in long-horizon adversarial decision making.
